previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of two kidney transplants was admitted with fever, chills, and foul-smelling urine. She was diagnosed with E. coli bacteremia and pyelonephritis. Treatment with intravenous antibiotics was initiated, later narrowed to ceftriaxone. Her immunosuppressant mycophenolate mofetil was temporarily reduced and later restored. During admission, she developed a vitreous hemorrhage in the right eye due to diabetic retinopathy, requiring photocoagulation. She also developed painful oral lesions suspicious for herpes simplex virus, prompting a course of acyclovir. A midline was placed for outpatient IV antibiotic administration. Her infection resolved, vital signs stabilized, and she was discharged home with follow-up plans for infectious disease, ophthalmology, dermatology, and transplant team.
problems: Pyelonephritis as a complication of transplant
Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
